forces.title: Shift towards zero-emission truck components in aftermarket
forces.description: The European MHDT aftermarket is undergoing a significant structural transformation as zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) rapidly gain market share. ZEV sales are projected to reach 46% of the EU HDT market by 2035, creating a new, high-growth aftermarket segment for specific ZE truck components. This necessitates component manufacturers and aftermarket distributors to develop new capabilities, expertise, and training for high-voltage diagnostics and battery health monitoring to support these evolving product lines.
forces.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

forces.title: Robust growth in aftermarket for traditional replacement parts and tires
forces.description: The EU medium- and heavy-duty truck (MHDT) aftermarket is a resilient and predictable revenue pool, estimated at €52.1 billion in 2025 and projected to grow to €56.7 billion by 2035. Replacement parts constitute a dominant 86% of this profit pool, with tires accounting for 14%. This sustained demand, driven by an aging fleet (average age over 14 years), provides a stable and profitable environment for auto component manufacturers and aftermarket distributors focusing on conventional parts.
forces.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

forces.title: Chinese OEMs' cost advantage and rapid innovation challenge European suppliers
forces.description: Chinese truck OEMs are entering the European market with a significant structural cost advantage of 30-40%, driven by large-scale battery production, faster R&D cycles (22-28 months vs. 40-48 months for Europeans), and innovative offerings like advanced battery packs and AI-native cockpits. This fierce competition, coupled with their ability to offer integrated energy solutions, poses a substantial risk to European auto component manufacturers, particularly in the EV battery and advanced electronics segments.
forces.source_title: Competing against Chinese innovation speed in European trucking

forces.title: Slow ZE truck adoption delays scale benefits for component suppliers
forces.description: European zero-emission (ZE) truck registrations remained below 5% as of 2025, despite the availability of over 45 ZE models. This slow adoption rate delays the realization of cost efficiencies at larger volumes for component manufacturers, such as those from dedicated battery-cell production lines. This directly impacts the profitability and growth potential of European component suppliers focused on ZE powertrains and related technologies, hindering investment in new production capabilities.

forces.title: Growth in autonomous truck technology creates demand for advanced components
forces.description: Autonomous trucks and buses are set to fundamentally change road freight and urban mobility in Europe, with commercial availability of driverless hub-to-hub applications expected by 2031. This revolution creates a €100 billion value pool by 2035, driven significantly by software, but also requiring advanced sensors (LIDAR, radar, cameras), computing hardware, and specialized wiring harnesses. This offers significant upside for component manufacturers specializing in these high-tech systems for autonomous vehicles.
forces.source_title: Mastering autonomous truck technology in Europe

forces.title: Shift towards integrated offerings for life cycle value in trucking
forces.description: The trucking industry's business model is shifting from purely hardware sales to integrated life cycle services, with customers increasingly expecting bundled packages that include vehicle provision, fleet management, charging, predictive maintenance, and uptime guarantees. This structural change necessitates component suppliers to adapt their offerings and potentially collaborate more closely with OEMs to provide integrated solutions, moving beyond discrete transactions and focusing on service-enabling components.
forces.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

forces.title: Revised EU Vehicle Dimensions directive benefits heavy component integration
forces.description: The ongoing revision of the European Vehicle Dimensions directive is expected to allow higher gross vehicle weights. This regulatory change is crucial as it can largely mitigate operational disadvantages stemming from the additional weight imposed by large EV battery packs and hydrogen storage vessels. This acts as a significant tailwind for manufacturers of these heavy components, making their integration into zero-emission trucks more feasible and enhancing the overall competitiveness of such vehicles.

forces.title: Customer hesitation and liability concerns hinder AV truck component demand
forces.description: Despite the significant potential of autonomous vehicles, only 36% of European fleet buyers expressed readiness to adopt AV trucks in 2026, up from 25% in 2025. Key concerns include unclear legal liability, lack of comprehensive regulations, and limited exposure to reliable autonomous operations. This customer hesitation directly slows the demand for advanced components specific to autonomous driving, creating uncertainty and potentially delaying return on investments for component suppliers in this high-tech segment.
forces.source_title: Mastering autonomous truck technology in Europe

forces.title: Need for ZEV service readiness impacting aftermarket operations
forces.description: The transition to zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) necessitates building comprehensive ZEV service readiness, which includes developing high-voltage diagnostics, specialized technician training, and advanced battery-health monitoring systems. This capability investment, largely funded by existing internal combustion engine (ICE) aftermarket cash flow, represents a structural change for aftermarket distributors and parts manufacturers, requiring significant upfront investment in expertise and infrastructure to effectively support future ZEV component servicing and maintenance.
forces.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

forces.title: Inadequate charging infrastructure limits ZE truck component adoption
forces.description: A critical barrier to widespread zero-emission (ZE) truck adoption in Europe is the severe shortage of charging infrastructure. Only about 2,000 public fast-charging points are currently available, a small fraction of the 15,000-20,000 needed by 2030, and 200,000 depot charging points required. This significant infrastructure gap directly constrains the market penetration of ZE trucks, thereby limiting the demand and growth opportunities for associated EV battery packs and other electric powertrain components.

forces.title: Increasing economic competitiveness of ZE trucks drives component demand
forces.description: For approximately 30% of the European truck market, zero-emission vehicles (ZEVs) already offer a total cost of ownership (TCO) advantage. This economic attractiveness is expected to grow, with 60% of fleet operators willing to switch at TCO parity, and up to 80% if ZEV TCO is 10% lower than diesel. This improving economic viability directly stimulates demand for ZE truck components, including EV battery packs and hydrogen fuel cell components, driving market penetration and volume for suppliers.

viewpoints.title: European OEMs face pressure from ZE truck transition delays
viewpoints.description: European OEMs are under increasing pressure due to slow adoption of zero-emission (ZE) trucks, with new registrations remaining below 5% as of 2025. This delay risks economic costs from missing efficiency leaps at larger volumes, such as those from dedicated battery-cell production lines, and potential CO2 penalties from EU emission standards. This implies a cautious outlook for European auto component suppliers tied to ZE technology as market scale-up is delayed, impacting demand for new EV battery packs and other ZE parts.

viewpoints.title: Chinese OEMs' cost advantage threatens European auto component manufacturers
viewpoints.description: Chinese truck OEMs are rapidly expanding into Europe, leveraging a significant 30-40% structural cost advantage. This stems from large-scale battery production, faster R&D cycles (2x faster), and lower overheads. Their innovative offerings, including advanced battery packs and AI-native smart cockpits, coupled with integrated energy solutions, pose a substantial competitive threat to European auto component manufacturers, particularly those involved in EV battery packs, advanced electronics, and powertrain components.
viewpoints.source_title: Competing against Chinese innovation speed in European trucking

viewpoints.title: Aftermarket services critical for European trucking profit pools
viewpoints.description: Vehicle sales are projected to represent only about 90% of Europe's truck-related revenue pool by 2035, with the remaining 10% coming from various life cycle services. These services, including aftersales (replacement parts, tires), are expected to constitute approximately 90% of total profit pools due to their significantly higher profitability. This highlights a strong positive outlook for aftermarket distributors and auto parts manufacturers as the industry increasingly focuses on recurring, high-margin revenue streams from the installed base.
viewpoints.source_title: Capturing life cycle value in Europe’s trucking industry

viewpoints.title: Autonomous truck technology shifts value to software, impacting hardware components
viewpoints.description: The advent of autonomous heavy-duty trucks in Europe is expected to create a €100 billion value pool by 2035, fundamentally shifting the industry's focus. This value will primarily move from hardware sales to high-margin software for autonomous functions, remote teleoperations, and predictive maintenance services. While this indicates a major opportunity for software providers, it implies a structural change and challenge for traditional hardware-focused auto component manufacturers, requiring a pivot towards advanced sensor technology and computing units.
viewpoints.source_title: Mastering autonomous truck technology in Europe
